name: US inflation
summary: FRED index data imply US CPI inflation of about 4.1% in October, up from 4.0% and inside the 3.0–4.5% Watch band
state: FRED CPI index data imply annual US consumer price inflation of about 4.1% in October, up from 4.0% in September and rising for three consecutive months, inside the 3.0–4.5% Watch band and below the 4.5% Alert line (FRED). No newer figure was available on 19 Nov; November CPI is due in mid-December.
for_you: Prices in the US are rising faster than a year ago, led by energy. Higher US inflation tends to keep US interest rates and borrowing costs elevated, with knock-on effects for global markets and the dollar.
rubric_hit: CPI 4.1% y/y within 3.0–4.5% Watch band; rising 3 months

sources.title: FRED — Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPIAUCSL)

why: Inflation sets Fed policy and thus global borrowing costs; a resurgence would keep rates high for everyone.
drivers: Energy, tariffs, wages, housing costs, supply chains.

rubric.watch: CPI 3.0–4.5%, or rising for 3 consecutive months.
